relations.note: Áine is consistently identified as Eogabal’s daughter in the principal Knockainey tradition.
Aillén is Áine’s brother or fellow child of Eogabal.

relations.myth: Áine arranges Aillén’s union with Uchtdelbh
relations.note: Áine learns Aillén’s grief and helps bring him together with Uchtdelbh.
Áine loves and kisses Manannán, who takes her when Uchtdelbh joins Aillén.
Modern summaries sometimes call Áine Manannán’s daughter, conflicting with their medieval partnership.
Áine’s embrace of Manannán prompts Uchtdelbh to notice Aillén and leave Manannán.
Later genealogical summaries sometimes make Eogabal’s son Fer Fí Áine’s brother.
A possibly different Áine is named as the Dagda’s daughter.

relations.myth: Áine dies for love of Banba
relations.note: A death notice says one Áine died for the love she gave Banba.

relations.myth: Fenian Áine loves and marries Fionn
relations.note: A namesake Áine loves or marries Fionn and sometimes bears his children.
A probably distinct Fenian Áine and Milucra are described as sisters.
Áine and Milucra compete as rival sisters in love with Fionn.

relations.myth: Fairy hosts contest land or harvest
relations.note: Later folklore places Áine’s and Donn’s fairy hosts in territorial conflict.

relations.myth: Fairy bride bears the enchanted Earl
relations.note: Fitzgerald folklore makes Áine mother of the magical or enchanted Gearóid Iarla.

relations.myth: Áine helps the Tuatha Dé Danann
relations.note: Localized folklore says Áine helps them if the hill receives her name.
